description: Which type of segmentation divides consumers by age - income - and gender?
explanation: Demographic segmentation uses measurable population characteristics like age - income - gender - education level - and family size to divide the market.
choice0: Demographic segmentation
choice2: Geographic segmentation
choice3: Behavioral segmentation

description: At which stage of the product lifecycle does competition tend to be highest?
explanation: Competition is highest during the Maturity stage because many competitors have entered the market and sales growth has leveled off.
choice0: Introduction
choice2: Growth
choice3: Decline

description: A company sets its price just below a round number (e.g. \$9.99 instead of \$10). This is an example of:
explanation: Psychological pricing (also called charm pricing) exploits the consumer tendency to perceive \$9.99 as significantly less than \$10.
choice0: Cost-plus pricing
choice2: Psychological pricing
choice3: Premium pricing

description: A company decides to sell its product exclusively through its own website. This is a decision about which element of the marketing mix?
explanation: Selling exclusively through a company's own website is a distribution/Place decision - part of the marketing mix.
choice0: Product
choice2: Promotion
choice3: Place

description: What is the difference between a brand name and a trademark?
explanation: A brand name is the spoken part of the brand identity. A trademark is a legally registered brand name or symbol that gives the owner exclusive rights.
choice0: A brand name is the spoken identifier; a trademark is the legally protected version
choice1: A trademark is used informally; a brand name is registered with the government
choice2: A brand name is only used in advertising; a trademark is used on packaging
choice3: There is no difference; both terms mean the same thing

description: Which digital marketing metric measures the percentage of website visitors who leave after viewing only one page?
explanation: Bounce rate measures the percentage of visitors who navigate away from the site after viewing only one page without further interaction.
choice0: Click-through rate
choice2: Conversion rate
choice3: Impressions

description: Maslow's hierarchy of needs arranges needs from most basic to highest. Which level comes immediately after physiological needs?
explanation: According to Maslow - after physiological needs (food - water - shelter) are met - safety needs (security - stability) are the next priority.
choice0: Self-actualization
choice2: Safety needs
choice3: Social needs

description: Which research method is best suited for gathering in-depth qualitative insights from a small group of consumers?
explanation: Focus groups are ideal for gathering in-depth qualitative insights - allowing a moderator to explore attitudes - opinions - and motivations in a group setting.
choice0: Large-scale online surveys
choice2: Retail sales tracking
choice3: Focus groups with a trained moderator

description: Which element of the promotion mix involves a sales representative personally meeting with a prospective customer?
explanation: Personal selling involves direct face-to-face interaction between a sales representative and a potential customer to persuade them to buy.
choice0: Personal selling
choice2: Public relations
choice3: Direct mail

description: What is the role of a wholesaler in a distribution channel?
explanation: A wholesaler buys large quantities of goods from manufacturers and sells them in smaller quantities to retailers - acting as an intermediary.
choice0: Selling directly to end consumers
choice1: Buying from manufacturers and selling to retailers in smaller quantities
choice2: Manufacturing goods for retailers to sell
choice3: Advertising products on behalf of manufacturers

description: A company sells its existing product to new geographic markets. Which Ansoff strategy does this represent?
explanation: Market development involves taking an existing product into new markets (e.g. new geographic regions or new customer segments).
choice0: Market penetration
choice2: Market development
choice3: Product development

description: In a SWOT analysis - which category would 'a new competitor entering the market' fall into?
explanation: A new competitor entering the market is an external factor that could negatively affect the business - making it a Threat.
choice0: Strength
choice2: Opportunity
choice3: Threat

description: What is a 'perceptual map' used for in marketing?
explanation: A perceptual map visually plots how consumers perceive brands in relation to two or more attributes - helping identify positioning opportunities.
choice0: Visualizing how consumers perceive competing brands on key attributes
choice1: Mapping the geographic distribution of customers
choice2: Tracking social media engagement over time
choice3: Showing the stages of the customer purchase journey

description: What does 'value-based pricing' mean?
explanation: Value-based pricing sets the price primarily based on the perceived value of the product to the customer rather than the cost of producing it.
choice0: Adding a fixed markup to production costs
choice1: Setting price based on how much value the customer perceives
choice2: Matching competitors' prices exactly
choice3: Using promotional discounts to increase sales volume

description: A luxury car brand targets consumers who value status and exclusivity. What type of segmentation is being used?
explanation: Psychographic segmentation targets consumers based on lifestyle - values - attitudes - and social status - which drives luxury brand purchases.
choice0: Demographic segmentation
choice2: Psychographic segmentation
choice3: Behavioral segmentation

description: What is brand extension?
explanation: Brand extension is when a company uses an established brand name to launch a new product in a different category.
choice0: Refreshing an existing brand's visual identity
choice1: Merging two brands after a corporate acquisition
choice2: Increasing advertising spend for an existing product
choice3: Using an existing brand name to launch a product in a new category

description: What is the primary goal of a 'conversion' in digital marketing?
explanation: A conversion occurs when a website visitor completes a desired action - such as making a purchase - signing up for a newsletter - or filling out a form.
choice0: A visitor completing a desired action such as a purchase or signup
choice1: A visitor sharing a page on social media
choice2: A visitor reading more than three pages on a site
choice3: A visitor returning to the site within 30 days

description: The influence of celebrities and athletes on purchasing decisions is an example of which type of social influence?
explanation: Celebrities and athletes function as aspirational reference groups - people we aspire to be like - and their endorsements influence consumer behavior.
choice0: Family influence
choice2: Cultural influence
choice3: Situational influence

description: Which marketing strategy is most appropriate during the Growth stage of the product lifecycle?
explanation: During Growth - the focus shifts to building brand preference - differentiating from new competitors - and expanding distribution to capture growing demand.
choice0: Heavy price discounts to attract first-time buyers
choice1: Reducing advertising spend to cut costs
choice2: Building brand preference and expanding distribution
choice3: Cutting production and preparing for discontinuation

description: What is the difference between quantitative and qualitative research?
explanation: Quantitative research collects numerical data measurable statistically - while qualitative research gathers descriptive data about attitudes and opinions.
choice0: Quantitative asks 'why'; qualitative counts how many
choice1: Qualitative uses surveys; quantitative uses interviews
choice2: Quantitative is cheaper; qualitative is more accurate
choice3: Quantitative collects numerical data; qualitative collects descriptive insights

description: Which promotional tool involves earning unpaid media coverage through press releases and news stories?
explanation: Public relations earns unpaid media coverage by managing relationships with the press and generating news stories - as opposed to paid advertising.
choice0: Public relations
choice2: Sales promotion
choice3: Sponsorship

description: A hotel offers a 'book early and save 20%' deal. Which element of the marketing mix does this relate to?
explanation: Early booking discounts are a pricing tactic - involving decisions about the price element of the marketing mix including discounts and special offers.
choice0: Product
choice2: Place
choice3: Promotion

description: What is an 'indirect' distribution channel?
explanation: An indirect channel uses one or more intermediaries (such as wholesalers or retailers) between the manufacturer and the final consumer.
choice0: Selling through the company's own stores only
choice1: Selling via the company's website directly
choice2: Selling through intermediaries such as wholesalers and retailers
choice3: Selling directly to business customers

description: What is a 'market leader'?
explanation: The market leader is the company with the largest market share in a given industry or product category.
choice0: The first company to launch a product in a market
choice1: The company with the highest profit margin
choice2: The company with the most employees
choice3: The company with the highest market share in its industry

description: What does Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) measure?
explanation: Customer Lifetime Value estimates the total net profit a company expects to earn from a customer over the entire duration of their relationship.
choice0: The total net revenue a business expects from a customer over time
choice1: The cost of acquiring one new customer
choice2: The average value of a single customer transaction
choice3: The number of times a customer buys per year

description: Which segmentation variable would a company use to target consumers who regularly buy its product more than once a week?
explanation: Usage rate is a behavioral segmentation variable - dividing customers into light - medium - and heavy users based on how often they buy or use a product.
choice0: Demographic segmentation by income
choice2: Psychographic segmentation by lifestyle
choice3: Geographic segmentation by city size

description: What is a 'private label' (or store brand) product?
explanation: A private label product is manufactured by one company but sold under a retailer's own brand name (e.g. a supermarket's own-brand cereal).
choice0: A luxury product sold in exclusive boutiques
choice1: A brand that only sells products online
choice2: A product made and sold by the same manufacturer
choice3: A product manufactured by one company and sold under a retailer's brand name

description: What is 'pay-per-click' (PPC) advertising?
explanation: PPC is a digital advertising model where advertisers pay a fee each time one of their ads is clicked - rather than paying for impressions.
choice0: Paying a flat fee to display an ad for one month
choice1: Paying based on the number of people who see an ad
choice2: Paying influencers for social media mentions
choice3: Paying each time a user clicks on an ad

description: The process by which individuals acquire the buying knowledge and experiences they apply to future purchase behavior is called:
explanation: Consumer socialization is the process through which people learn skills - knowledge - and attitudes relevant to their behavior as consumers.
choice0: Consumer socialization
choice2: Brand association
choice3: Selective perception

description: Which Ansoff strategy carries the MOST risk?
explanation: Diversification - introducing a new product into a new market - carries the highest risk because the company has no existing experience in either dimension.
choice0: Market penetration
choice2: Market development
choice3: Product development

description: Which component of SWOT analysis deals with internal factors that put a company at a disadvantage?
explanation: Weaknesses are internal factors within a company that reduce its ability to achieve objectives - such as limited resources or poor brand recognition.
choice0: Opportunities
choice2: Weaknesses
choice3: Strengths

description: A brand positions itself as the most affordable option in its category. This is an example of which positioning strategy?
explanation: Positioning by price/value highlights that the product offers the best deal - focusing on affordability as the key differentiator.
choice0: Positioning by product attribute
choice2: Positioning by competitor
choice3: Positioning by price and value

description: What is 'competitive pricing'?
explanation: Competitive pricing involves setting prices based primarily on what competitors are charging for similar products - rather than on costs or demand.
choice0: Setting prices in line with what competitors charge
choice1: Setting prices based on production cost plus a profit margin
choice2: Setting prices based on what consumers are willing to pay
choice3: Temporarily reducing prices to beat a specific competitor

description: What is the purpose of test marketing?
explanation: Test marketing involves launching a product in a limited area to gauge consumer response before a full-scale launch - reducing the risk of failure.
choice0: Testing a product's durability in laboratory conditions
choice1: Launching a product in a limited area to measure consumer response before full launch
choice2: Surveying employees about a proposed new product
choice3: Analyzing secondary data about market size

description: A company redesigns its product packaging to make it more eco-friendly. This is a change to which element of the marketing mix?
explanation: Packaging is considered part of the Product element in the marketing mix - as it relates to how the product is presented and its physical attributes.
choice0: Price
choice2: Product
choice3: Place

description: What is the key difference between advertising and personal selling?
explanation: Advertising is a mass communication paid for by the sponsor - while personal selling involves direct one-on-one interaction between a salesperson and a prospect.
choice0: Advertising is cheaper per contact; personal selling reaches more people
choice1: Advertising requires a large budget; personal selling is always free
choice2: Advertising is only digital; personal selling happens in stores
choice3: Advertising is mass communication; personal selling is direct one-on-one interaction

description: What does 'organic reach' mean in social media marketing?
explanation: Organic reach is the number of people who see content without paid promotion - through natural sharing - followers - and algorithmic distribution.
choice0: The number of people who see content without paid promotion
choice1: The total number of followers an account has
choice2: The number of times an ad is shown to paid audiences
choice3: The engagement rate on sponsored posts

description: What is 'co-branding'?
explanation: Co-branding is a partnership between two or more brands that feature both brands' identities on a single product or marketing campaign.
choice0: Licensing a brand name to a foreign manufacturer
choice1: Collaborating with another brand on a joint product or campaign
choice2: Updating a brand's visual identity every few years
choice3: Extending a brand into a new product category

description: A consumer buys a cheaper store-brand cereal instead of a name brand. This behavior is most closely associated with:
explanation: Price sensitivity is the degree to which price affects consumer purchase decisions. Choosing a cheaper substitute shows high price sensitivity.
choice0: Brand loyalty
choice2: Price sensitivity
choice3: Cognitive dissonance

description: What is 'intensive distribution'?
explanation: Intensive distribution means placing a product in as many outlets as possible to maximize availability and convenience for consumers.
choice0: Selling only through a single exclusive retailer
choice1: Selling directly to consumers online only
choice2: Selling through a carefully selected network of premium outlets
choice3: Placing a product in as many retail outlets as possible

description: What does 'market share' measure?
explanation: Market share is the percentage of total sales in a market that a company controls - calculated by dividing the company's sales by total market sales.
choice0: A company's sales as a percentage of total market sales
choice1: The number of customers a company has compared to competitors
choice2: The profit margin a company earns relative to the industry average
choice3: The number of products a company sells in a given period

description: Which of the following actions would most directly INCREASE a customer's lifetime value?
explanation: Customer lifetime value increases when customers buy more frequently - spend more per transaction - or remain loyal longer. Reducing churn (stopping customers from leaving) extends the relationship.
choice0: Offering a one-time discount to new customers only
choice1: Reducing customer churn through a loyalty rewards program
choice2: Increasing advertising spending on social media
choice3: Launching a new product for a completely different market

description: A company emphasizes that its running shoes are endorsed by Olympic athletes. This is an example of positioning by:
explanation: Positioning by user associates the product with a particular type of user or aspirational group - in this case elite athletes - to attract consumers who identify with that image.
choice0: Product attribute
choice2: User imagery
choice3: Competitor contrast

description: What typically happens to the price of a product during the Decline stage of the product lifecycle?
explanation: In the Decline stage - companies often reduce prices to sell remaining inventory and maintain some volume as demand drops.
choice0: Prices increase as remaining loyal customers pay a premium
choice1: Prices stay the same to maintain brand image
choice2: Prices fluctuate unpredictably due to market volatility
choice3: Prices are often reduced to clear remaining inventory

description: A streaming service creates different subscription plans for students - individuals - and families. This is an example of:
explanation: Offering different pricing tiers for different segments is market segmentation combined with targeted product/price differentiation.
choice0: Targeting distinct customer segments with tailored plans
choice2: Behavioral segmentation by viewing history only
choice3: Competitive pricing against rival streaming services

description: When a manufacturer offers a rebate to encourage the purchase of a specific product - this is part of which 'P'?
explanation: Rebates are a form of sales promotion - which falls under the Promotion element of the marketing mix.
choice0: Product
choice2: Price
choice3: Place

description: What is 'rebranding'?
explanation: Rebranding is the process of changing a company's or product's image - name - logo - or positioning to better reflect its current identity or target a new market.
choice0: Launching a brand in a new international market
choice2: Changing a brand's name - logo - or image to better fit new goals or audiences
choice3: Increasing advertising spend to boost brand awareness

description: Which of the following is an example of secondary data?
explanation: Secondary data is data that already exists and was collected for another purpose. Published industry reports are a classic example of secondary data.
choice0: A telephone interview conducted with 50 customers
choice1: An in-store observation of shopping behavior
choice2: A new survey sent to your mailing list
choice3: Published industry reports from a trade association

description: A growing trend toward healthy eating represents which component of SWOT for a fruit company?
explanation: A growing consumer trend toward healthy eating is an external positive trend that the fruit company can exploit - making it an Opportunity.
choice0: Opportunity
choice2: Weakness
choice3: Threat

description: What is 'influencer marketing'?
explanation: Influencer marketing involves partnering with individuals who have a large and engaged social media following to promote a brand or product to their audience.
choice0: Paying large media companies for TV ad slots
choice1: Partnering with social media personalities to promote products to their followers
choice2: Running targeted email campaigns to industry professionals
choice3: Sponsoring online news articles about your brand
